title: The sprint manager measures each change's test impact and schedules heavy runs by it
goal: testmap.py impact, given paths or an item id, prints the test files the item's touches select, their share of all test files, a cost estimated from per-test-file durations that a full tests.py run records, and one tier (narrow, gate or checkpoint) with its reason; backlog.py plan and start print it per item; kb-sprint orders ready items by it (items that select all first) and after each landing a backlog.py subcommand sums the landed impact since the last heavy run and says when a heavy run is due (a landed item that selects all, or a sum past the threshold the story's gate sets); that heavy run is the sprint's checkpoint and the run before review stays mandatory.

gates.question: When is a heavy run (stress_test.py with the full tests.py) due in the middle of a sprint? Recommended: when a landed item selects all test files, or the landed items' selected test files since the last heavy run pass half of all test files.
options: An item that selects all, or landed impact past half of all test files
Only an item that selects all
Every fifth landing of a _tools/ item
gates.recommendation: An item that selects all, or landed impact past half of all test files
gates.answer: An item that selects all, or landed impact past half of all test files

notes: testmap.py already builds the import graph in-process with ast (reach, deps, explain, select), so the impact measure extends it. kbingest map's PythonMapper runs python -m ast in a subprocess per file, isolated for untrusted repositories; it is not reused, since this repository is trusted and its maps are slower; other languages are out of scope. Impact inputs: the test files a path selects (all for conftest.py, tests.py, pyproject.toml and unknown paths), a module's fan-in (the test files that reach it), and per-test-file durations written by a full tests.py run. A heavy run due mid-sprint replaces a fixed cadence: ST-tbi3rras's bisect then spans only the landings since that run.
